events.title: An ode to instantons
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: An ode to instantons
events.detail_text: Abstract : We will review a formalism for real time evolution in quantum theory in the semiclassical limit, using the path integral. The motivation is to understand non-perturbative transitions in QFT in situations with interesting time dependence. We will illustrate how it works for the decay of a coherent state trapped in a metastable region in quantum mechanics. At the end we briefly speculate on the extension to QFT. Based on [2603.06575], [2605.04139]

Their intrinsically narrow minibands, achieved by twisting or aligning atomically thin two-dimensional crystals, favor strong electronic interactions. Additionally, electrostatic gating further enables in situ control of carrier density, bandwidth, and bandgaps, stabilizing a wide range of quantum phases, including superconductivity, correlated insulating states, ferromagnetism, and Chern and fractional Chern insulators. Most experimental knowledge of these systems has come from quantum transport, scanning-probe, or optical experiments in the linear-response regime. This work extends the experimental toolbox by employing cryogenic nonlinear optoelectronic methods. By applying such techniques to graphene moiré materials, we probe two regimes that remain difficult to access with conventional experiments: the quantum geometry of interacting flat bands and the out-of-equilibrium states generated by large in-plane currents. events.title: A quasi-star is born: Formation and evolution of accreting quasi-stars as a pathway to Little Red Dots
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: A quasi-star is born: Formation and evolution of accreting quasi-stars as a pathway to Little Red Dots
events.detail_text: Abstract : Little Red Dots (LRDs) are a population of compact, luminous sources discovered by JWST at high redshift, whose nature and origin remain under debate. One possible explanation involves quasi-stars: massive stellar envelopes surrounding rapidly accreting black holes. This talk will explore the formation and evolution of quasi-stars from rapidly accreting primordial and low-metallicity stars, and their potential connection to the observed properties of LRDs. The evolution from supermassive stars to black-hole-hosting quasi-stars will be discussed, together with their lifetimes, masses, luminosities, and effective temperatures. The results suggest that quasi-stars can reach properties compatible with those inferred for LRDs, providing a possible link between the formation of massive black holes and this newly discovered population of high-redshift sources.

events.title: Closed and open questions in secondary gravitational waves
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Closed and open questions in secondary gravitational waves
events.speakers: Guillem Domènech, Institute for Theoretical Physics - Leibniz University
events.detail_text: Abstract : Primordial fluctuations in the early universe generate secondary gravitational waves. Detecting a cosmic gravitational wave background would present a direct window into primordial physics. In this talk, I will review the production of secondary gravitational waves and present new results, including a solution to the gauge issue and a universal prediction for chiral gravitational-wave backgrounds. I will end by discussing an interesting open question on secondary gravitational waves from scalar-tensor mixings.

events.title: LEONID PONOMARENKO SEMINAR: Negative mobility and Landau diamonds in graphene
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: LEONID PONOMARENKO SEMINAR: Negative mobility and Landau diamonds in graphene
events.speakers: Negative mobility and Landau diamonds in graphene
events.detail_text: Seminars October 20, 2026 LEONID PONOMARENKO SEMINAR: Negative mobility and Landau diamonds in graphene Hour: From 11:00h to 12:00h Place: Elements Room Share Outlook iCalendar Google SEMINAR: Negative mobility and Landau diamonds in graphene LEONID PONOMARENKO Lancaster University I will discuss two distinct transport phenomena in high-mobility monolayer graphene. The first concerns the Dirac electron–hole plasma that forms near charge neutrality at elevated temperatures. Analysis of longitudinal and Hall resistivities reveals strong Coulomb drag: majority carriers pull minority carriers along with them, reversing their expected drift direction and producing negative mobility. I will discuss the competition between electron–hole collisions and scattering by phonons and impurities, and its implications for a hydrodynamic description of the Dirac plasma. The second part will present unpublished experiments on nonlinear transport in the low-temperature Shubnikov–de Haas regime. Maps of differential resistivity versus carrier density and DC Hall voltage reveal diamond-shaped regions of low resistance, termed Landau diamonds, and a bias-induced reversal of the oscillation phase. Measurements on devices of different widths support the Hall voltage as the controlling parameter in this experiment. I will discuss an interpretation based on the tilting and overlap of Landau bands in the Hall electric field and the use of diamond boundaries to estimate Landau-level spacings. Hosted by

events.title: MATHEUS CAPELA SEMINAR: Entropic limitations on fixed causal order
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: MATHEUS CAPELA SEMINAR: Entropic limitations on fixed causal order
events.speakers: Entropic limitations on fixed causal order
events.detail_text: Seminars October 20, 2026 MATHEUS CAPELA SEMINAR: Entropic limitations on fixed causal order Hour: From 12:00h to 13:00h Place: Seminar Room Share Outlook iCalendar Google SEMINAR: Entropic limitations on fixed causal order MATHEUS CAPELA University of Rochester The causal structure of physical processes is usually assumed to be fixed: events occur in a definite order, even when the underlying quantum systems exhibit nonclassical correlations. Quantum theory, however, allows for more general processes in which the causal order itself can be indefinite, as exemplified by the quantum switch. This raises a fundamental question: can the causal structure of a process be characterized purely in terms of the information it can transmit? In this talk, I will discuss an information-theoretic approach to this question based on information inequalities. We derive a class of inequalities that must hold for any process compatible with a fixed causal order, including both definite causal orders and classical mixtures thereof. Their violation therefore provides a sufficient condition for certifying genuinely non-fixed causal order. Remarkably, the framework is not restricted to the von Neumann entropy, but extends to a broad class of information measures, including Rényi entropies. When characteristic dimensions become comparable to relevant physical length scales, optical, electrical, chemical and thermal responses can differ significantly from those of the corresponding bulk materials. Controlling matter at these scales therefore provides a powerful route to engineer functional surfaces and materials, but also requires fabrication processes capable of controlling dimensions, morphology and interfaces at the nanometre scale. This seminar will focus on a nanofabrication route based on ultra-thin metal films (UTMFs) and their transformation into nanostructured glass surfaces. The process starts with the deposition of continuous metallic films only a few nanometres thick, where film nucleation, growth and the use of seed layers become particularly relevant. events.title: The unintuitive SU(3) flavor and chiral limits of hadron resonances
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: The unintuitive SU(3) flavor and chiral limits of hadron resonances
events.venue: Pere Pascual 540 Room, 5th floor, and via Zoom
events.detail_text: Abstract : Contrary to naive expectations, poles used to define hadron resonances rigorously in the physical world may not evolve continuously to become degenerate in the SU(3) flavor and chiral limits of QCD. Instead, other shadow poles, usually ignored, may be the ones that degenerate and characterize the resonances in these limits. This feature is general, and we illustrate it first with the simple and familiar light-vector mesons, followed by the much-discussed light-scalar case. Their shadow poles and their degeneracy are found using the QCD low-energy effective theory unitarized to one loop. Based on: 2606.14634

events.detail_text: Insight Seminar October 22, 2026 DAFEI JIN INSIGHT SEMINAR: Quantum Information on Quantum Matter Hour: From 12:00h to 13:00h Place: Elements Room Share Outlook iCalendar Google INSIGHT SEMINAR: Quantum Information on Quantum Matter DAFEI JIN Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Notre Dame ABSTRACT: Noble-gas atoms, such as helium and neon, condense into quantum liquids and solids at low temperatures. They are the purest forms of matter in nature, free of chemical contamination or electromagnetic noise, and can serve as ideal hosts for quantum information carriers. In this talk, I will present our series of developments over the past few years, in trapping electrons and atoms on noble-gas quantum matter and manipulating their quantum states by on-chip electronics and optics. Our research has established new platforms for quantum computing, networking, and sensing. BIO: Dafei Jin is an Associate Professor of Physics and Electrical Engineering at the University of Notre Dame. His research lies at the intersection of quantum matter and quantum information. He pioneered the development of quantum information platforms based on electrons and atoms trapped on noble-gas quantum solids. He is a recipient of the 2021 Julian Schwinger Foundation Award for Physical Research, the 2024 Department of Energy Early Career Award, and the 2026 Moore Foundation Experimental Physics Investigator Award. events.title: Solving perturbative gravitational dynamics by recursion
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Solving perturbative gravitational dynamics by recursion
events.detail_text: Abstract : Surprisingly, tools from quantum field theory can with advantage be used to solve the Einstein field equations perturbatively. The formalism is recursive in nature, building each new order from combinations of terms already computed at lower orders. For black hole backgrounds the series can be evaluated to infinite order, thus giving first examples of gravitational perturbation theory yielding exact answers.

events.title: Spreading Solar Energetic Particles in the Heliosphere: Multi-spacecraft observations
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Spreading Solar Energetic Particles in the Heliosphere: Multi-spacecraft observations
events.venue: DAM 7.24 Seminar Room and via Zoom
events.speakers: David Lario, Heliophysics Science Division, NASA, Goddard Space Flight Center
events.detail_text: Abstract : Solar energetic particle (SEP) events are enhancements in energetic particle intensities observed by spacecraft (S/C) in interplanetary (IP) space originating from solar eruptions. SEP events are commonly classified into two classes: Impulsive and Gradual. Impulsive SEP (ISEP) events are small short-lived intensity enhancements resulting from magnetic reconnection processes associated with solar coronal jets. Gradual SEP (GSEP) events are large and long-duration enhancements associated with fast and wide coronal mass ejections (CMEs) capable of driving shocks that efficiently accelerate particles. A distinguishing feature of ISEP events is their relatively narrow longitudinal spread compared to the broader spread of GSEP events. Early observations by near-Earth S/C suggested that ISEP events were confined to a narrow (~30°) range of longitudes around the site of the solar eruption origin of the SEP event. In contrast, GSEP events are observed to spread over a wide range of heliolongitudes. Recent multi-S/C observations using more sensitive instruments have revealed that ISEP events can exhibit broader longitudinal spans than previously thought, and that GSEP events can occasionally span a full 360° around the Sun.
